title: So Many Days, So Much Praise
raw_text:
The prose in SO MANY DAYS is almost poetic, it's rhythmic, and it's wise.

It has lovely illustrations of a girl and her puppy making their way through various seasons and places together, she in a raincoat and galoshes. The simple coloring and style is very reminiscent of the story books I loved as a child in the 60's, soothing yet playful.

The best part of the book is its message that you are stronger, braver and wilder than you know, and an important part of a big, beautiful world waiting to be explored. It asks the question "Who will you be and where will you go? And how will you know?" and even says "Sometimes you won't". Yet it still encourages the reader to wonder about all the possibilities and ends with saying "You are loved more than you know".

The message may be a bit beyond the average young child, but certainly is worth passing on. I actually have decided this would be a nice little something for my daughter who is graduating from college and would recommend it as a cute, unique book for all graduates (perhaps with a little something tucked inside).

title: Great Plot...Horrible Writing!
raw_text: The Plot is decent and the drama leaves you wanting more. However, the authors' writing skills are mediocre at best. I hate when published books have typos because if I spend my money buying a book, the author should at least have the decency to proof read it. Also, the Haitians have a half Jamaican/half weird accent that irritates me to my core; authors please do your research!! Respect culture, you should have consulted with Haitians before you butchered their accent. The same goes for the Murder mama from the islands, her accent was also terrible. Additionally, drama is always good but the trilogy borders the line between artful and unrealistic. At times it seems like there is just too much going on. There are obviously creative minds behind the trilogy however, your writing/grammar skills and cultural knowledge leave a lot to be desired.

title: Vibrant Colors with a Dark Storyline
raw_text:
"Oh No" is something that I wouldn't usually say when reading a comic but this time I did... that is when I had finished, I wanted more you see!

With its gloriously vibrant colours mixed with a dark storyline this is another great offering from DC Entertainment which will immerse you. From Alfred's snarky comments on Bruce's behaviour to the taunting and goading from Gotham's less morally compassed foes.

The story is set prior to Arkham Knight and gives us an insight into the cat and mouse relationship between Batman and his nemesis, and how it develops into the infamous ongoing dual for good over evil, where it seems one cannot live without the other.

This novel contains some excellent and exclusive artwork and the hardback is a true keepsake to fans of the game series.

Thanks to DC Entertainment and NetGalley for the ARC of this book in return for my review.

title: A Book Worth Buying
raw_text:
I won't say this is perfect literature, but I thought it was a suspenseful story, and I enjoyed it enough to actually buy two copies of it. I gave one away. If you like post apocalyptic types of stories, and you like Christian fiction, then you might like this one. In this book the characters are dealing with the "hard times" many people believe Revelation says will come before "The Second Coming." I like books about people resorting to sustainable/survivalist living, and I like Christian stories that reflect on God's love and provision. This story fulfilled both criteria. It is due a second read.
I gave it five stars because I just haven't found a book that is quite like it.

title: Tense page turner with things that go bump in the night....
raw_text:
This item was given to me for my review.
The Quick, by Lauren Owen, is a tense read that kept me wanting to both find out what happens next and close the book and not look again. The setting is Victorian England, but not the pleasant BBC England we love on the tellie. No, this is the England of Jack the Ripper and foggy streets and things that go bump in the night. This England is dark and brooding and dangerous. The characters are set in place slowly, and, at times, I was anxious for the author to just get on with it, but the technique did add that tension I mentioned earlier, and allowed it to build. The style of writing reminded me of 19th century authors, and I mean that in a positive way. This really added to the Gothic flavor I felt the novel had. Though there was no castle, per se, the whole of London lent itself as the creepy setting. There is not romance in the traditional sense, but there is a love story here, and heroes and heroines and good versus evil. However, the author addresses the story elements with craft and style, and I definitely think that if you like suspense, the supernatural and horror with things that make you jump, and you like a novel that is also well written, then this is a new author to try.
